content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Timothy Wallace (E022) requests admin access to Payroll.

Notes:
- Most notes say: role Engineer, full_time employee. Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist (not Engineer). Full-time max is write unless role owns system. Requested admin exceeds max → recommend write.
- Note 6 (Security DB) says: contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read unless advanced training (then write); never admin. Requested admin exceeds max → recommend read.

There's a conflict: most agents say full-time → max write. Security says contractor → max read.

The employee is an Engineer. The system is Payroll, owned by Payroll Specialist role.

Policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

For Engineer on Payroll: If full-time, max is write (they don't own Payroll). If contractor with basic training, max is read.

The conflict between full-time and contractor. Which to trust? The security DB note says contractor with basic training, noting it differs from other agents' full-time assumption. Compliance DB confirms Engineer; team memory indicates full-time.

Hmm. This is a discrepancy. As Approver, I need to decide. There's conflicting evidence about employment type. Most notes (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) say full-time. Security says contractor.

Which is more authoritative for employment type? Typically HR would be the authority on employment type. Note 1 (probably HR?) says full-time. The Security DB note says contractor. 

Actually, let me consider. The team memory doesn't specify which agent wrote which note, but note numbers correspond to tickets? It says "6 note(s) about employee E022" and each note is labeled ticket 1 (all from ticket 1? weird). Actually all notes are from ticket 1 - meaning multiple agents wrote notes on this same ticket. Note 6 is from Security DB showing contractor.

Employment type conflict: HR/IT/Finance/Compliance/Facilities say full-time; Security says contractor. HR is typically the source of truth for employment type. The majority says full-time.

Given full-time Engineer requesting admin to Payroll: max = write (role doesn't own Payroll). Requested admin > max, so grant max = write.

So decision: write.

Evidence: Employee is full-time Engineer, Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist, so admin not allowed; max is write. Grant write (maximum, below requested admin which is above max).

Let me submit write.
